findings.reason: the plan should add a node routing clones.py's git runner, revision reader and cache root through velocity.py (or record a retained-exception reason), exactly as §10 did for interface_counts.py.
findings.text: clones.py carries its own `_git` (line 644), its own revision-source reader `revised_python` (line 652, reading every `.py` at a revision through `git archive` + tarfile) and its own cache-root resolver `_cache_root` (line 389), each duplicating a mechanism the plan's own §10 promoted to a public owner in reckon/velocity.py (`git` line 147, `read_blobs`/`read_trees` line 360, `velocity_cache_root` line 542) and merged interface_counts.py onto — so §4's module is left as a parallel copy of the readers §10 established, and the two revision-source readers (ls-tree + batched `cat-file` in interface_counts vs `git archive` in clones) can drift apart silently

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — reckon/_timestamps.py hides the whole parsing policy (Z suffix, offset, naive-as-UTC, epoch seconds/milliseconds split at 1e11, malformed-returns-None) behind `parse_utc` and `parse_iso`, and reckon/_store.py's `write_atomically` hides the sibling-temporary/fsync/chmod/rename sequence behind one callback-taking function; neither spreads its behaviour across many small wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — reckon/clones.py keeps a private git runner, a `git archive` revision reader and a cache-root resolver beside the velocity.py owners that §10 named for exactly those three roles.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; the one open section (§11) adds no definition and states so in its own text, no section adds a CLI option, MCP view or refusal code, and the sections that add public functions (§2, §3, §4, §5) each name the helpers/callers they merge or carry interface accounting.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan is built on a structural census (§1 names 44 direct `fromisoformat` callers, 14 divergent atomic writers, three stream enumerators, four identical decoders) and §10 explicitly merged interface_counts.py's private reader, cache root and git wrapper onto velocity's public `read_blobs`/`velocity_cache_root`/`git`, so it cites the machinery it searched rather than asserting it.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — `write_json_atomically` (reckon/_store.py:477) layers JSON serialisation, parent creation and per-caller defaults (indent, sort_keys, ensure_ascii, mode, create_parents) over `write_atomically`, documenting each keyword; it specialises the owner rather than wrapping existing machinery without cause.
